title: What is a Motorized Sewing Machine?
path: What is a Motorized Sewing Machine?
text: A motorized sewing machine is a fast sewing machine used in tailoring and garment industries. The balance of wheel is attached to the motor with a belt. There is a treadle which when pressed with foot helps to run the machine. It works using an electric motor. The motor is connected to the balance wheel using a belt. A foot pedal (treadle) is used to control the speed. When you press the pedal, the machine starts running.

title: Types of Sewing Machines
path: What is a Motorized Sewing Machine? >  Types of Sewing Machines
text: Motorized sewing machines are classified based on the type of stitch they produce. Lock Stitch Machine Chain Stitch Machine

title: Lock Stitch Machine
text: Lock stitch machines are the most frequently used for ready to wear apparel production. Lock stitch machine is the common machine used in domestic tailoring and industrial production. The stitch is formed by interlocking two threads. This machine is distinguished by the winding device provided for the bottom thread (Bobbin thread).

title: Single Needle Lock Stitch Machine
path: Lock Stitch Machine >  Single Needle Lock Stitch Machine
text: This machine has a needle thread as well as a bobbin thread for the loop formation purposes. Loop formation of this machine occurs according to the interloping terminology.

title: Methodology behind the loop formation
path: Lock Stitch Machine >  Methodology behind the loop formation
text: The formation of a stitch begins when the needle penetrates the fabric and descends to its lowest point. The bobbin hook then slides by the needle’s scarf, catching the upper thread, and carries it around the bobbin thread. The thread is then pulled up into the fabric, completing the stitch.

title: Double Needle Lock Stitch Machine
path: Lock Stitch Machine >  Double Needle Lock Stitch Machine
text: This machine has two needle threads and two bobbin threads to form lock stitch. Double needle lock stitch machines stitch formation is same as single needle lock stitch machine but forms two lock stitches which are parallel to each other.

title: Chain Stitch Machine
text: This machine is specially designed for attaching waistbands to garments such as jeans and casual pants. It can handle two types of waistband styles. Pre-cut waistband Continuous band style It provides accurate stitching and strong, durable seams, which are very important in chain stitching operations. Chain stitch machines use special under threads called looper threads, which are supplied from large thread cones. In this machine, the stitch is formed using a continuous series of loops, creating a chain-like structure. It can be identified by A thread tension device mounted on the machine arm Absence of a spool winder

title: Care and Maintenance
text: Clean the machine regularly. Oil the machine for smooth working. Cover the machine when not in use. Remove dust and thread pieces before oiling. Use a soft brush or cloth for cleaning.

title: Introduction to Over lock Machines
text: An overlock machine, also known as a serger, is a specialized sewing machine that uses multiple threads to finish the edges of fabric unlike a standard sewing machine, an overlock machine uses loopers instead of a bobbin, and it trims the seam allowance as it stitches to create a neat, professional – looking seam. Overlock machines a special purpose machine used for finishing edges and sometimes for seaming. It falls under the class 500, which means stitches are formed with one or more groups of threads and have a general characteristic that loops from at least one group of threads pass around the edge of the material. Overlock sewing machines are usually runs at high speeds, from 1000 to 9001 rpm and mostly are used in industry for edging, hemming and seaming a variety of fabrics and products. Overlock stitches are also used for decoration, reinforcement or construction. Overlock machines come in different models but all are basically similar.

title: Parts of the machine
path: Introduction to Over lock Machines >  Parts of the machine
text: Needle bar Thumb screw (to regulate pressure of the presser foot) Thread cutter Presser foot Needle Tension set (for needle) Tension set (for over looper) Tension set (for under looper) Cloth plate Slide cover Hand wheel (rotates in clockwise direction) Feed ration Sight glass (or) window Indicates lubrication of the mechanism Indicates the level of the oil in oil tank Lower and upper knife Lower and upper knife are fixed in the opposite direction with the sharper edges meeting each other so that the fabric will get cut each movement sharp edges of the knife overlap around 0.5 – 1 mm depth. The overlock machine has two feed dogs, the main feed dog and the differential feed dog. The levels of these two should be equal with one another and the height can be adjusted independently by the respective bolts. The height of the feed dog must be adjusted according to the thickness of the material. Feed ration nut regulator increases and decreases the teeth of the feed dog to get shirring and stretching stitches. Threading of Over lock machine Threading of the overlock machine is strictly complicated compared with other sewing machines.

title: Methodology behind the stitch formation
path: Introduction to Over lock Machines >  Methodology behind the stitch formation
text: When the needle enters the fabric, a loop is formed in the thread at the back of the needle. As the needle continues its downward motion into the fabric, the lower looper begins its movement from left to right. The tip of the lower looper passes behind the needle and through the loop of thread that has formed behind the needle. The lower looper continues along its path moving toward the right of the serge. As it moves, the lower thread is carried through the needle thread. While the lower looper is moving from left to right, the upper looper advances from right to left. The tip of the upper looper passes behind the lower looper and picks up the lower looper thread and needle thread. The lower looper now begins its move back in to the far left position. As the upper looper continues to the left, it holds the lower looper thread and needle thread in place. The needle again begins its downward path passing behind the upper looper and securing the upper looper thread. This completes the overlock stitch formation and begins the stitch cycle all over again.

title: Types of Overlock stitches
text: Overlock machines are generally made in 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 thread formations. Each formation has unique uses and benefits. One thread Overlock End to end seaming or butt seaming of piece goods for textile finishing. Two thread overlock Stitch type 503, machine has one needle and one looper. A two-thread model is best for finishing seam edges and decorative edgings, or finishing edges for light fabrics. It can also be used to stitch flatlock seams. It can be used to stitch elastic and lace to lingerie. Stitches can be adjusted to sew rolled hem. Three thread overlock Stitch type 504, Machine has one needle and two loopers. A three-thread overlock trims, stitches, and overcasts seam in one operation. The three-thread overlock seam is most useful when sewing knits. It can be used to sew woven fabrics, but not in areas that will receive a lot of stress. Some three-thread models can be converted to do two-thread stitching. This is a most common over edging having excellent stretch and recovery. Here stitches looks the same on the both the sides. Four thread Overlock Machine has two needles and two loopers. The four-thread overlock will stitch a chain stitch or a safety stitch as it stitches and overcasts seams. The chain stitch model is most useful when seaming woven fabrics. The safety stitch model can be used to sew woven or knitted fabrics. Machine can be converted to two thread or three thread Overlock. Five thread Overlock Machine has two needles and three loopers. It is two thread chain stitch combined with a three thread overlock. The left needle and lower looper for two thread chain stitch. For every unit length of stitch, it requires 20 times of thread length.
